title: ChemInform Abstract: Chemistry and Structure of Phosphides and Polyphosphides. Part 50. K4P3, a Compound with the P4‐ 3 Radical Anion.
abstract: AbstractSingle crystals of the title compound are mechanically separated from the product of the reaction of red phosphorus with excess potassium (400 °C, Nb‐ampoules, argon atmosphere; attention the K: P > 1 product can decompose explosively).
